attributes.probed_form: THREE SOURCE EDITS, all in src/game/game/player.c, commit 9182a748f. (1) static inline f32 player_scale_att(f32* att, f32* range): `return 0.01 * *att * (range[1] - range[0]) + range[0];` -> `return 0.001 * ...`. This ONE helper is inlined into BOTH reported callers, which is why PlayerProcessPowerups and PlayerUpdateAtts each reported the identical `target 0.001 / ours 0.01` pair twice; there is no separate bug in either caller. (2) create_player_blits: all SEVEN `mbBlitCvtCoord(<blit>, 0.1f)` calls -> `mbBlitCvtCoord(<blit>, 64000.0f)` (frame_blit, rune_blit, crystal_blit, key_blit, rune13_blit, hod_blit, quest_blit). (3) create_player_blits: `MBOX_FindTexture_Err("HODICON", NULL, 1)` -> `MBOX_FindTexture_Err("RUNE13", NULL, 1)`. WHY THE SET DETECTOR WAS DECISIVE, and this is the reusable part: PlayerProcessPowerups also emitted two ALIGNED_MISMATCH rows (target 0.0f / ours 100.0 and target 100.0 / ours 0.0f) that the SET detector did NOT report, because both sides read both values; those are pairing artifacts and were correctly left alone. Conversely the whole-function set for PlayerUpdateAtts was literally `lfd:0.001 x2` against `lfd:0.01 x2` with nothing else to slide against, which is as clean as this evidence class gets.

attributes.verification: GROUND TRUTH read from the split listing, not from the detector's own decode: build/GUNE5D/asm/auto_11_80345D70_sdata2.s declares `lbl_80347828: .double 0.001`, `lbl_80347748: .float 64000` and `lbl_80347A48: .string "RUNE13"`. CORROBORATION for each: (1) attributes feeding player_scale_att are capped at 999.0f by check_player_atts (target lbl_80347994 = .float 999), so 0.001 maps a 0..999 attribute onto the 0..1 range the class-range interpolation needs and 0.01 overshoots by 10x; (2) the same TU already calls mbBlitCvtCoord with 64000.0f at three other sites (src lines 759, 990, 997), so 64000.0f is this function's established coordinate scale; (3) a byte scan of build/GUNE5D/main.retail.dol finds "RUNE13" at 1121782 and "BTMBK_LEVL" at 1118472 but finds "HODICON" NOWHERE IN THE IMAGE (find returned -1), so our string could not have been the original under any spelling, and the target asm at 0x8007C8A0 loads lbl_80347A48 into r3 for the MBOX_FindTexture_Err call that feeds the hod_blit MBCreateBlit at 0x8007C894. VALUE AUDIT (the arbiter this class requires, run before and after over the same unit): cs_constsweep.py on game/game/player went ALIGNED_MISMATCH 43 -> 35 and SLIDE_SUSPECT 29 -> 25, closing 12 rows, and the set-detector VALUE_MISMATCH row for all three functions disappeared entirely. Every one of the 12 'new' rows in the after-run is a pre-existing row whose anonymous pool index shifted by one (@3516->@3517, @3906->@3907, @2224->@2225 and so on), i.e. renumbering, not a new defect.
